previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and chest discomfort following a missed dialysis session. She had a history of paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, systolic dysfunction, and mitral regurgitation. On admission, she was in normal sinus rhythm but had fluid overload, hyperkalemia, and a supratherapeutic INR. A chest X-ray showed small bilateral pleural effusions and bibasilar atelectasis. She underwent hemodialysis, which resolved her symptoms and normalized her potassium. Her metoprolol dose was reduced due to bradycardia and lightheadedness, and warfarin was held due to elevated INR, with plans to restart at 2mg daily. She was discharged home in stable condition with medication adjustments and follow-up arranged with cardiology.

She is taken to the OR with Dr ___. At the time of 
surgery, no complications were reported.  The kidney pinked up 
upon anastomosis however it did not make any urine, but it had 
good pulsations and good color. The patient also underwent 
fascial component separation with Marlex mesh, and ventral 
hernia repair following the kidney placement.
Immediately post op, in the PACU the patient initially c/o ___ 
pain. She was also noted to be in AFib with rapid ventricular 
response, which she has a history of (on coumadin). Morphine PCA 
was initiated.
Post OP labs revealed a potassium of 6.7 and the patient was 
emergently dialyzed in the ICU where she had been transferred. 
Esmolol x 1 and then amiodarone drip were started. 
The patient was kept in the ICU through POD 2. The heart rate 
stabilized and she was switched to home dose amiodarone PO and 
also home dose metoprolol.
She was transferred to ___ 10 on POD 2 following a second round 
of hemodialysis.
When transferred to the floor she was noted to again be in AFib 
and was complaining of jaw pain and some arm heaviness. Vital 
signs remained stable, enzymes were cycled and negative, EKG 
revealed AFib with RVR. Cardiology came by n continued consult, 
and recommended IV lopressor in addition to PO dosing. The rate 
was controlled however she remained in AFib for a majority of 
the hospitalization. Mildly symptomatic with chest 
""palpitations"" but otherwise stable.
Initial urine output was poor with less than 50 cc daily for the 
first 4 days.
Aftetr POD 3 she was ___ hyperkalemic, and although weight as up 
about 15 kg, her respiratory status was stable.
On POD 5 the kidney started making more urine and by POD 7 she 
made 750 cc. Creatinine was 6.5 then 6.6 prior to discharge 
without HD so appeared to be stabilizing.
Routine immunosuppression was initiated, however she received 
and additional dose of ATG for 4 x ___ mg. Solumedrol taper per 
protocol. FK was started on POD 1 in the eveing. FK level on 
discharge was 11.6 and dose was dropped to 5 mg BID. 
Cellcept was giving marked heartburn so she was switched to 
Myfortic prior to discharge with seemingly good relief of that 
GI complaint. New script was called in and she had the Myfortic 
at discharge.
Additionally, her coumadin was restarted prior to discharge as 
it was determined there would not be a kidney biopsy due to 
increasing urine output. Her PCP, who is ___ ___ MD will be 
following INRs as he was prior to transplant.
Patient was kept on home dose levoxyl during this 
hospitalization. Due to AFib, a TSH was sent which came back low 
at .2, however the free T4 and T4 were WNL. The patient was 
encouraged to follow up with PCP regarding dosing and recheck 
once out of the hospital.

function and was tolerating regular (low potassium) diet.

radiology_notes.text:
CHEST

HISTORY:  End-stage renal disease.  Preop for kidney transplant.

TWO VIEWS:  The right costophrenic sulcus is not included.

Comparison with the previous study of ___.

The lungs now appear clear except for minimal streaky density at the lung
bases consistent with subsegmental atelectasis or scarring.  The heart is
within normal limits and size.  The aorta is mildly tortuous.  Mediastinal
structures are otherwise unremarkable.  The bony thorax is grossly intact.

IMPRESSION:  No active disease.

HISTORY:  ___ female with new right IJ catheter placement.  Patient
status post renal transplant.

COMPARISON:  Preoperative chest radiograph from ___.

PORTABLE AP CHEST RADIOGRAPH:  The tip of a new right internal jugular
catheter projects over the expected location of the mid SVC.  The nasogastric
tube tip is within the stomach.  Mild vascular congestion and widening of the
cardiomediastinal contours is new compared to prior.  Subsegmental bibasilar
atelectasis and probable small effusions are noted.  There is no focal
consolidation or pneumothorax.

IMPRESSION:
1.  New right internal jugular catheter, tip at mid SVC.  No pneumothorax.
2.  New mild vascular congestion and mediastinal widening.
3.  New bibasilar atelectasis and probable small effusions.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with right kidney transplant today and no urine
output.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and color Doppler ultrasound images of the right iliac
and kidney was obtained.

COMPARISON:  There are no comparison studies available.

FINDINGS:
The right kidney transplant measures 11.2 cm without evidence of
hydronephrosis or perinephric fluid collection.  
The main renal artery and main renal vein waveforms are normal and patent. 
The upper, mid and lower pole intrarenal arterial waveforms demonstrate normal
systolic upstrokes with resistive indices ranging from 0.60 to 0.83. A small
anechoic lesion is seen at the lower pole of the transplant kidney, compatible
with a simple cyst.  The urinary bladder is not visualized.

IMPRESSION:
1.  No hydronephrosis and no perinephric fluid collections.
2.  Normal venous and arterial waveforms in the transplant kidney.
